#1766. 'Am I supposed to answer that?': Erling Haaland breaks silence and distances himself from Man City cheating verdict as star striker insists 'I don't really know much... I was playing for Bryne Under 9s'

Published: 09:50 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 06:26 EST, 16 November 2026

Erling Haaland delivered a monologue of over two minutes detailing the teams he represented in the years covered by the Premier League's investigation into Man City, as the star questioned how he was meant to respond to the club's guilty verdict.

Man City were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing when the verdict was released in September. The club have since appealed.

An independent commission ruled Man City had disguised payments worth £900million in a nine-year period with ‘sham’ deals.

Man City were found to have artificially inflated sponsorship agreements and pumped money into the club from its Abu Dhabi owners via disguised payments in a bid to swerve Premier League spending rules.

Haaland was quizzed about the club's situation by Norwegian broadcaster TV2, after scoring in the national team's 3-1 victory over Wales on Saturday.

The Man City star's initial answer lasted for two minutes and 14 seconds, as he reeled off the teams he had represented from 2009 to 2018, the years covered by the charges.

Erling Haaland insisted it was difficult for him to answer a question about Man City's guilty verdict, with the club appealing against the decision of an independent commission. Source: TV2Sport

Haaland stressed he remains happy at the club after being asked about his future given the potential ramificiations if Man City fail with their appeal to overturn the verdict.

'In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2013, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don't need the whole list. 2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team,' Haaland began.

'Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne's first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

'So this is a question I struggle to answer because it's a legal battle…

'It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with. Am I supposed to answer that? I'm not really sure.'

Haaland continued by listing fellow Norwegians who had been at Man City at the time, joking that they may be in a better place to offer insight.

'There were quite a few Norwegians at the club during that period, I think,' Haaland said.

'Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen and Omar Elabdellaoui were there. Kjetil Haug was there too. I think there were a couple more but I can't remember.

The forward distanced himself from the case as he listed team he played from 2009-18, the time covered by the charges. Pictured: Haaland in action for Molde in 2018

'But it's a difficult question to answer when I don't really know that much about it.

'I assume the answers will come… I don't know when. I haven't read much about it.

'To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City.

'A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022 and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that says everything about the matter. I'm a City player, and I'm incredibly happy there.'

Man City have continued to insist they had 'irrefutable evidence' proving their innocence, but if the club loses its appeal, the Premier League have a range of sanctions at their disposal – including relegation or expulsion.

Haaland, who has won eight major honours at the club including the Treble in 2023, was asked about whether the case has affected his thoughts on his Man City future.

'I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said, I signed a long-term contract in 2024,' Haaland responded.

'I'd say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that. I won't say it myself, but look at the trophies I've won and how I've developed on and off the pitch.

'I'm standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we're top of our group in Europe.

'Things aren't going so well for City in the league, but we'll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can't focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark.'

Man City have won twice and lost three times in the Premier League since the independent commission verdict was announced in September.

Enzo Maresca's side have slipped to six points behind reigning champions Arsenal following their drop off in form.

#1764. Coventry City vs. Crystal Palace: Head-to-head record and past meetings before Premier League clash

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 22:55

Coventry City welcome Crystal Palace to the Coventry Building Society Arena this weekend in a crucial Premier League relegation clash following the November international break.

Frank Lampard's 17th-placed Sky Blues sit just one point above the bottom three after a 3-1 defeat at Everton, though October home wins over Newcastle United and Sunderland offer encouragement as they chase consecutive top-flight victories on their own turf.

Meanwhile, new Palace boss Thomas Frank takes charge for the first time with less than a week of training under his belt, tasked with ending a four-match losing run and lifting the London club above their West Midlands hosts.

Here, Sports Mole takes a closer look at the head-to-head record and past meetings between Coventry and Crystal Palace.

Over 118 years have passed since Coventry City and Crystal Palace first locked horns - an FA Cup tie in January 1908 that ended in a 4-2 victory for the Eagles - and there have now been 114 competitive meetings between the two clubs across all competitions.

There is very little to separate the sides historically, with the Sky Blues holding the narrowest of edges on 41 victories, while Palace are hot on their heels with 38 wins and another 35 encounters have ended all square.

More than 14 years have elapsed since their most recent clash in March 2012, when the two teams shared the spoils in a 1-1 Championship draw in the West Midlands several months after Palace had edged a 2-1 victory at Selhurst Park.

Coventry's last triumphs in this fixture came during the 2010-11 campaign, when they recorded back-to-back 2-1 home wins in the FA Cup and Championship in January and February 2011 to avenge a 2-0 defeat in South London earlier that season.

Prior to that double, Palace had enjoyed a dominant spell over the Sky Blues, putting together a 10-match unbeaten run across all competitions between September 2005 and November 2009 that included seven wins and three draws.

That sequence featured five consecutive victories for the Londoners - highlighted by emphatic 4-1 and 4-2 away triumphs - before Coventry finally ended their hoodoo with a gritty 1-0 win at Selhurst Park in February 2010.

This weekend's showdown marks their first Premier League meeting in over 28 years, with the clubs last crossing paths in the top flight in February 1998 when Coventry ran out 3-0 winners in South London.

Across their six previous Premier League encounters, the Sky Blues hold the upper hand with two victories to Palace's one alongside three draws, and remarkably neither side has ever won a home game in the competition.

Palace's lone Premier League success in this fixture was a 4-1 away demolition in November 1994, whereas Coventry claimed 2-0 and 3-0 victories on the road in February 1995 and February 1998 respectively.

Before the Premier League era, Coventry were a formidable force against Palace in the old First Division, going unbeaten in their first 14 top-flight meetings between 1969 and 1990 - winning 10 and drawing four - before the Eagles finally broke their duck with a 2-1 win in December 1990.

Knockout meetings have been rare, with Palace winning three of their four cup ties - including 3-0 and 1-0 League Cup successes in 2002 and 2005 - while Coventry's most emphatic results in the fixture date back to their Division Three (South) days in the 1930s, when they dished out 8-0 and 8-1 home thrashings in 1932 and 1935.

#1763. Mourinho stands firmly behind Vinicius amid Real Madrid scrutiny

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Jose Mourinho has once again called Vinicius Junior "an incredible player" following a positive international break for the Real Madrid winger.

Vinicius has struggled for Los Blancos this season, scoring just once and providing three assists in 12 appearances across all competitions.

The 26-year-old also missed Madrid's last four LaLiga matches before the break after receiving a straight red card for a hair pull against Villarreal.

However, during the international break with Brazil, Vinicius scored a brace against Japan before netting a hat-trick against Singapore.

Ahead of Madrid's league meeting with Celta Vigo, Mourinho reiterated his support for Vinicius.

"Starter, off the bench, or in the stands, it doesn't matter," Mourinho said about Vinicius' role in the team.

"It's a strange thing because, a couple of weeks ago, people were talking about Vinicius as if he were the huge problem Real Madrid had, and after scoring goals against Singapore and Japan, we can't stop talking about Vinicius: if he plays, if he doesn't, why he has to play.

"I think it's too much. What I say about Vinicius is what I've said one, two, three, four, and five weeks ago: he is an incredible player, we love him, we need him, we have always tried to help him, and that's what we will continue to do.

"Here, we don't have players with privileges. We don't have players who have to play by decree. We have a group of people working for the team, for Real Madrid."

@ViniJr  @BellinghamJude https://t.co/HgVQCrRx8F

— Real Madrid C.F.  (@realmadriden) November 20, 2026

Madrid are second in LaLiga, three points behind early leaders Barcelona, ahead of welcoming 11th-place Celta to the Estadio Bernabeu.

Celta are one of five opponents Mourinho has faced on more than one occasion in LaLiga with a 100% win rate (W2), alongside Athletic Club (W6), Rayo Vallecano (W5), Hercules (W2) and Real Valladolid (W2).

"Celta are much better than the points they have," said Mourinho. They are a team that last season beat us here, at the Bernabeu.

"They are playing in Europe, and perhaps playing matches on Thursdays and then in the league is also costing them some points, but this factor does not exist [for this fixture].

"They will surely present themselves as always: organised and ambitious. They concede few goals because, defensively, they are very organised, and they know how to do it and how to press."

Kylian Mbappe has scored in each of his last seven appearances for Madrid in all competitions (nine goals) and could equal his best scoring run for the club, achieved between September and October 2025 (eight games, 12 goals).

Williot Swedberg has scored more LaLiga goals against Madrid than against any other side (four in five games).

Since the start of 2024-25, he has been involved in five league goals against Madrid (four goals, one assist), the joint-most alongside Raphinha.

Madrid have lost just one of their last 24 LaLiga games against Celta (W21 D2), a 2-0 defeat in December 2025, winning 11 of the last 12.

Los Blancos have won their last eight games in all competitions, their best winning run since a 10-game streak between May and September 2022 under Carlo Ancelotti.

However, Madrid lost their last home game against Celta in LaLiga and have only twice lost consecutive home games against them in the competition (L2 in 1943 and in 2006).

Celta have picked up points in six of their last seven away games against teams from the Community of Madrid in LaLiga (W3 D3 L1), but they lost their most recent such match 3-0 against Rayo Vallecano last October.

Celta have conceded 10 goals and kept six clean sheets in LaLiga 2026-27, both their best records after the first 12 games of a season in the competition since 2002-03 (eight goals and seven clean sheets), under Miguel Angel Lotina.

#1762. Report: Six clubs interested in Milan midfielder Jashari including four domestic rivals

A number of clubs are interested in signing Ardon Jashari from AC Milan, according to a report from his native Switzerland.

Jashari has once again found himself playing largely as a back-up under Ruben Amorim this season, after performing the role of being Luka Modric’s deputy during his debut campaign with the Rossoneri under Massimiliano Allegri.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Given that over €30m was invested to sign him from Club Brugge, a bigger role and impact was perhaps foreseen by all parties. Thus, Jashari’s situation is one to monitor, and there is certainly no shortage of interested parties.

According to information from 4-4-2.ch, clubs in both Serie A and the Premier League are seriously considering a move for the 24-year-old midfielder, who started last night in Switzerland’s 4-0 win over Scotland and impressed.

Roma, Juventus, Atalanta and Como are the four Italian clubs that are looking at the Swiss international. From England, it is Aston Villa and Nottingham Forest that are monitoring his situation closely.

Jashari is under contract until 2030, so Milan have leverage, and they have not yet received a concrete offer. However, this could change as January gets closer. The Rossoneri still highly value Jashari, even though he hasn’t yet established himself as a regular starter.

A permanent sale would therefore require a fee in the range of €35-40m. Milan paid Club Brugge a similar sum for him a year ago and they have no intention of making a loss, given his age and potential.

#1761. Bradford City vs Doncaster Rovers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 23:09

Bradford City and Doncaster Rovers will square off on Saturday in a Yorkshire derby with importance at both ends of the League One table.

The hosts sit a point outside of the playoff places following a defeat last time out while their visitors have dropped into the bottom four due to consecutive losses.

Bradford City head into their first League One game of November at the weekend following an international break with the hopes of returning to winning ways and moving back into the top six.

After winning promotion from League Two and losing in the League One playoffs in the last two seasons, the Bantams picked up where they left off in early 2026-27, winning five of their first seven outings before Graham Alexander departed for Preston North End.

They then turned to Michael Duff and have struggled to continue their hot start since, winning one, drawing four and losing one of their last six league matches with the only victory coming against Stevenage in mid-October.

That did form part of a run of four straight clean sheets for the Bantams, who top the division with nine and have conceded a league-low tally of eight goals, but that came to an end in their last league outing against fellow promotion-chasers and Yorkshire rivals Huddersfield Town, who dished out a 3-0 beating at Mbanq Valley Parade.

Now, at least, on the back of a pair of confidence-boosting cup wins before their break, beating Marine 7-0 in the FA Cup and York City 4-0 in the EFL Trophy, Bradford City now sit eighth, but just two points off fourth spot, and will hope to retake a top-six spot and kickstart another hot streak in League One.

Their visitors, meanwhile, make the trip across Yorkshire in search of a return to winning ways of their own in their battle at the other end of League One.

Doncaster Rovers also won promotion from League Two in 2024-25 and finished 14th last time around on their return to the second tier but now find themselves 21st with just 12 points on the board from 13 games.

That is in no small part down to a poor away record, having lost five of seven games on the road, collected just four points and conceded 16 goals in those.

Two heavy away defeats have come consecutively for Grant McCann's side since a home victory over Sheffield Wednesday, as they lost 3-1 at Luton Town and 6-1 in their last third-tier match away at MK Dons at the end of October.

Having also since played two cup games, beating Rochdale in the EFL Trophy and losing 3-0 away at non-league Kidderminster Harriers in the FA Cup, Doncaster Rovers now head into a tough trip aiming to kickstart an upturn in form in League One and climb out of the bottom four.

Doncaster Rovers form (all competitions):

Bradford City remain without wide men Josh Neufville and Tyreik Wright, while attacker Bobby Pointon also missed their last outing through injury.

Corey O'Keeffe will continue in a wing-back role in Neufville's absence, while Antoni Sarcevic will start in midfield having served a suspension in the FA Cup for a red card received in their last league game.

George Lapslie, Adam Phillips and Nick Powell will all compete for starts in attack after Jake Beesley led the line with support from Kayden Jackson and Will Swan in the 3-0 defeat to Huddersfield.

Doncaster Rovers continue to contend with several injury issues, as James Collins, Francis Okoronkwo, Matty Pearson, James Husband and Tommy O'Reilly should all remain sidelined.

McCann made some rotations in their two cup games and should make changes from the team that lost 6-1 to MK Dons in their last league outing, with the likes of Robbie Gotts and Will Keane pushing to start after being reduced to substitute appearances.

Hakeeb Adelakun will also challenge for a start on the wing and may join Isaac Hutchinson and Jordan Thomas in support of a lone striker unless captain and key man Owen Bailey returns to an advanced midfield role.

McCracken; Pennington, Baldwin, Pratt; O'Keeffe, Sarcevic, Connolly, Touray; Swan, Beesley, Phillips

Doncaster Rovers possible starting lineup:

Simkin; Sterry, Grehan, Byrne, Senior; Broadbent, Gotts; Thomas, Bailey, Adelakun; Keane

Bradford City have certainly not been at their best in League One since Michael Duff's arrival, but still boasting the league's standout defensive record, and having rebuilt confidence with a pair of dominant cup wins, we back them to come out on top at home to a struggling Doncaster team.

#1760. 'Managers now are b****y boring!': NEIL WARNOCK on the lack of characters in football, his friendship with Pep Guardiola, why he is open to managing again post-Christmas - and how he almost became a chiropodist!

Published: 19:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 08:25 EST, 16 November 2026

Spending time in the company of Neil Warnock is always an education, be it witnessing one of his legendary foul-mouthed touchline rants or perched at one of his stage shows at grand venues like London Palladium.

On this occasion, Daily Mail Sport is perched in an east London bar watching on as one of English football's national treasures is posing for some modelling. Yes, you read that right, Mr Warnock is here to launch his own pair of socks with a tipple of Famous Grouse whisky in hand.

The complements on Warnock's 77-year-old feet are soon over, though, and we can get on to talking about a life in football that started six decades ago as a winger for Chesterfield and has traversed 10 clubs as a player, 17 as a manager and more than 2,000 games in the dugout.

So where to start? Maybe his reflections on nearly five decades in management – and how the whole conversation about feet is not too out of place…

'You don't realise how long it has been really, I started off just a team of ragamuffins as I call them,' he says in his iconic Yorkshire accent. 'They used to train on the green where I had digs in Hartlepool and asked me to coach them.

'I remember we scored from a set-piece we worked on, I was running up and down the touchline high-fiving everyone. I got the bug. I knew I could never get to the top as a player, I was quick but I was brainless.

Daily Mail Sport caught up with Neil Warnock to discuss his six decades in football

After representing 10 different clubs as a player, Warnock became one of the most compelling managers in the game

'I could've been a chiropodist if not in football. That could be on a quiz, couldn't it? I had bad feet at Scunthorpe, I used to get massive blisters so the physio there started getting me to do some of the players' feet.

'I enjoyed doing ingrown toenails and things like that! So I thought why not? Then I had a practice in Sheffield. I had to make a decision when we won the league at Scarborough whether to go full-time or pack it in. I thought, "Oh, go on then, let's give it a little go".

'It's not worked out badly, really, has it?

'People come up to me every day and say, "You're a legend, you". And I say, "Oh, thank you very much". Then they tell me what club they support, I have had so many haven't I? Last week I went out for a minute and had four selfies. They all appreciate what I did for their club.

'There aren't as many characters in the game now, you wouldn't get upset with managers now like in my day because now they are that b****y boring! Some of them barely speak.

'They won't get the rapport we had. I managed at a good time. The way I managed, I needed that humour. I needed the lads to enjoy it. I signed a lot of players that many managers wouldn't touch with a barge pole, are you with me? They ended up getting me promotions.'

The aforementioned humour brings us on to a private conversation he had with the great Pep Guardiola, one of the millions of anecdotes up Warnock's sleeve but one that he has not told until now.

'I went to a training session and he asked me to say a few words,' explains Warnock. 'I said, "Well lads I bet you're glad I'm not your manager because we'd be kicking balls from there to there, chasing it, heading it, practicing our tackles"... everyone laughed.

Warnock views Pep Guardiola as the best manager of his lifetime, while the Spaniard praised the veteran's humour after once addressing his Man City squad at a training session

Warnock has led teams to promotions on eight occasions over the course of his career

'After the session we had a coffee and Pep said to me, "Neil, that was amazing, you know when you talked to the players? I understood why you had so many promotions".

'He started counting and said, "What we have is all these staff… computers, details, nutritionist, all these staff, but you know what we don't have? Humour". He noticed why my lads had done well in my teams, just in that meeting. It was good, that. He is amazing.

'Pep is the best manager of my lifetime. They say he had all the best players but it is not easy managing them. Pep did things with players and now there are non-league teams trying to play like Manchester City!'

Warnock is now doing stage tours - Guardiola attended one last season - and had a tear in his eye when he stepped out at London Palladium given he used to watch shows there with his mother, who was in a wheelchair, on the TV as a child.

So what is Warnock up to these days? His current role is advisor at Torquay United but last management job was at Aberdeen two years ago… so is he out of the rat race for good this time?

'No, not really, no,' he says. 'I only work from February to April! So the phone will be on after Christmas. You never know, do ya? There will be someone thinking "why don't we get that Warnock in?".

'I've retired 40 times! Every time I have said it, I have meant it. But it's that dressing room camaraderie. There's something about football, when I look at some of the managers now… they just don't excite me.

'I remember Ruben Amorim (breaks down laughing). He's got his computer out on the bench! I remember watching and thinking, "I'm sorry, son, you need more than a computer to help you tonight!".

Warnock is currently doing stage tours, with Guardiola among the attendees last season

Warnock's current role is advisor at Torquay United and briefly served as interim manager last season, with the 77-year-old admitting he had not completely ruled out a return to the dugout

'And likewise, I see them making notes on the bench, oh my god. I think "what are you doing, your shopping list for Tescos?".

'I do enjoy walking and I enjoy photography, believe it or not. I go up the river with my phone, there's so many lovely things to see.

'I've got an electric bike and I sometimes do about 25 miles. I was thinking of doing a cycle of all my clubs but that would take me five years! They go at about 30mph down the hills, you've got to be careful, you wouldn't want to come off them.'

He is also enjoying fishing, being with the family and playing golf with his son, a PGA rising star William - though Warnock Sr insists he often embarrasses himself playing off 'the ladies' tee'.

The thing that makes Warnock most proud is the four promotions at Wembley but also the togetherness he fostered in his many teams.

He tells us: 'What I like about the teams I had, they all have reunions. You look at the tele now, someone will score a goal and kiss the badge… they won't have a reunion.

'When I go to these reunions, I see all my lads and how I blended that dressing room together and I look at the comradeship they still have now, they are the same as they were just a lot older.

'This year, my Scarborough team are having a 40-year celebration and the lads have invited me. I said there's no way I'm going out with that lot after the do because they can drink, let me tell you!'

Shoppers can pick up a free pair of colourful, collectable socks with selected 70cl bottles of The Famous Grouse whisky, priced from £18.50. Available in-store only, while stocks last.

#1759. ‘I’d rather go to the Champions League than win the derbies and finish 15th’, says Pellegrini

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Real Betis boss Manuel Pellegrini revealed he "would rather go to the Champions League and not win than win the derbies and finish 15th".

Betis take on rivals Sevilla in LaLiga on Saturday, with both sides looking to make a push for the Champions League places this season.

Betis are fourth after 10 games, seven points behind leaders Barcelona following a 2-0 win over Elche before the international break.

Sevilla, meanwhile, are eight points behind their rivals in sixth ahead of their clash at Estadio Ramon Sanchez Pizjuan.

Pellegrini has won two of his last three LaLiga games against Sevilla (D1), after failing to win any of his previous 10 (D6 L4). Away from home, he has only won three of his 15 matches against Sevilla in the competition (D3 L9).

The former Manchester City boss acknowledged the importance of the rivalry, but has bigger goals in mind for his Betis side.

"I expect Sevilla to have a clear, very direct style of football, they play in their own half and will be a very dangerous team," said Pellegrini.

"The approaches are different every year because the squads are different. Rivalry is always positive as long as it stays on the pitch and not off the field. We will try again to overcome them through our style of play.

"For the fans, winning all the derbies would be important. But if I had to choose, I'd rather go to the Champions League and not win than win the derbies and finish 15th.

"The most important thing is to get the three points. The best way to win is to maintain the same style of play we showed against other opponents. Playing away from home doesn't change our fundamental approach."

Lucien Agoume has regained possession 65 times in the 2026-27 LaLiga season; only Barcelona's Pedri (69) has completed more recoveries among outfield players in the competition this term.

Marc Bartra has scored three goals in eight LaLiga games this season; only Atletico Madrid's Alejandro Grimaldo (four) has scored more among all defenders in the competition this term.

Sevilla have lost two of their last three LaLiga matches against Betis (D1) after not losing any of their previous 12 against them in the competition (W7 D5).

Sevilla have also picked up points in 11 of their last 13 home LaLiga games against Betis (W9 D2 L2), although they lost the most recent meeting 2-0 in November 2025.

Betis are unbeaten in their last four away LaLiga matches (W2 D2), keeping clean sheets in their last two. They have not recorded three consecutive away clean sheets in the competition since October 2022 (W1 D2).

Sevilla have won just one of their last five LaLiga derbies against Andalusian teams (D1 L3). Betis, however, have lost only one of their last 14 derbies in the competition (W6 D7), but that defeat was against Sevilla (1-0 in October 2024).

Sevilla boss Luis Garcia has faced Pellegrini 11 times in LaLiga, more than any other coach (P11 W2 D4 L5), failing to win any of his last six meetings with him (D4 L2).

#1758. Feyenoord vs SBV Excelsior - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 19 Nov 2026 23:13

Feyenoord host SBV Excelsior at Stadion Feijenoord (De Kuip) in Rotterdam in round 13 of the 2026-27 Eredivisie on Saturday.

The Pride of South sit second in the Eredivisie table on 25 points, one behind PSV after losing 5-3 at Heerenveen on November 8, while Excelsior are 15th on 11 points, one clear of the relegation play-off place after five straight league defeats.

Giovanni van Bronckhorst's side arrive without a win in five matches in all competitions, having lost 1-0 at Real Betis on October 21, drawn 1-1 with PSV and Fortuna Sittard, lost 3-0 at home to Inter Milan on November 3 and lost 5-3 at Heerenveen.

Heerenveen was Feyenoord's first league defeat of the season, and it came after they led 2-0 through Anis Hadj Moussa and a Nacho Ferri penalty, only for substitute Ringo Meerveld to score a hat-trick.

Their attack has not been the problem, as 36 league goals in 12 games trail only PSV's 40, and a 5-0 home win over Utrecht on September 20 featured two goals from Hadj Moussa plus strikes from Ferri, Luciano Valente and Gaoussou Diarra.

The damage is coming at the other end, where Feyenoord have conceded seven goals in their last three league games after allowing 10 in the first nine, and they have let in at least one in each of their last five matches in all competitions.

Goalkeeper Tjark Ernst, signed from Hertha BSC for €5m in the summer, received sarcastic applause from home supporters after a routine catch against Inter, and Opta figures published by NOS rate only two Eredivisie goalkeepers worse than him at keeping out shots, although Van Bronckhorst continues to select him.

Captain Valente said after the Heerenveen defeat that things clearly had to change, while Van Bronckhorst has said that opponents have adapted to the way Feyenoord play.

Ruben den Uil's side won 4-0 at Cambuur in their opening game to go top of the Eredivisie for the first time in 47 years, and they had 10 points from five games after a draw at NEC on September 8.

Since then Excelsior have taken one point from a possible 21, a run of seven games that includes a 2-2 draw at Ajax on September 19 despite being outshot 33-8, a 1-5 home loss to Groningen and a 4-0 defeat at Heerenveen on October 16.

In their last five league games, Excelsior have conceded 20 goals and scored once, a stretch that includes a 9-0 defeat by Twente on November 1, the heaviest in the club's league history, in which Nesto Groen was sent off after five minutes for a challenge on Robin Propper.

Go Ahead Eagles then won 1-0 at Excelsior on November 7 through Soren Tengstedt, in a game Den Uil described as a typical 0-0, which left the Kralingers without a goal in four league games and on 16 for the season, four of which came in the opening win at Cambuur.

Aymen Sliti, who has three league goals, and defender Jan Plug are both on loan from Feyenoord, and Sliti has said he will not celebrate if he scores at De Kuip.

Feyenoord have eased the restrictions on visiting supporters for the derby, who will not be required to use organised transport to De Kuip.

Hadj Moussa is a major doubt after a sprained ankle on international duty with Algeria following the game against Togo, and Feyenoord-watcher Martijn Krabbendam said on Voetbal International's podcast that reaching the derby will be difficult, with the club aiming to have him ready for the Klassieker against Ajax on November 29, although Kicker reported that he left the Algeria camp after a dispute with the coach rather than through injury.

Jeremiah St. Juste is still out with a shin problem and Van Bronckhorst hopes to have him back before the winter break, while Bart Nieuwkoop, Jordan Bos and Thomas Beelen are not expected until after it and Tijme Wessels is recovering from knee surgery.

Reiss Nelson and Shaqueel van Persie are available again after injuries, Gijs Smal has returned to group training and Jakub Moder, who has played one minute this season, is also being eased back, although neither is certain for Saturday and no Feyenoord player is suspended.

For the visitors, Groen misses the derby serving the last game of a three-match ban, with one match suspended, for the red card against Twente, which leaves Mario Dominguez or David Garden to lead the line.

Sliti hurt his hand in the Netherlands Under-21s' 3-2 defeat by Denmark on November 17 and fears a bruised or broken thumb, but he has said he expects to play on Saturday, with former Feyenoord winger Alireza Jahanbakhsh the alternative on the flank.

Ernst; Read, Watanabe, Marmol, Lopez; Zechiel, Vanhoutte, Targhalline; Van Persie, Ferri, Valente

Van Gassel; Bos, Plug, Widell, Meissen; Yegoian, Hartjes; Naujoks, Thorsteinsson, Sliti; Dominguez

Feyenoord have won each of their last six meetings with Excelsior, scoring at least twice every time, including 2-1 wins on August 16, 2025 and March 15, 2026, and Excelsior have not won at De Kuip since 1980.

That record matters because this Excelsior side has conceded 20 goals in five league games, has lost Groen up front and faces an attack that has scored 36 times in 12 league games.

Feyenoord's own defence, which has conceded in five straight matches, and the possible absence of Hadj Moussa leave a small opening, but Excelsior have failed to score in each of their last four league games, so we expect Van Bronckhorst's side to win without needing to rely on one player.

#1757. More than just a football club: Cardinale’s vision to make AC Milan a multi-billion empire

In case you weren’t aware from his repeatedly bold comments in the media, Gerry Cardinale has big plans for AC Milan.

The RedBird Capital founder and chief has made one concept very clear: while he is at the helm, Milan are no longer just a football club, but a platform that aims to integrate sports, infrastructure, and entertainment. Of course AC Milan will be at the centre of the web, but the idea is to expand.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The proof of this comes from a three-letter acronym: MSE. It stands for Milan Sports & Entertainment and it is the new holding company created by RedBird. The idea, simply put, is to bring together investments and activities in various sectors under one umbrella.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport recall, Cardinale explained to the Financial Times that the assets involved could be valued in the mid-single-digit billions, meaning several billion dollars. So, how does he plan to get there?

Cardinale linked the creation of MSE to the process initiated with the acquisition of Milan: “Milan Sports & Entertainment is the culmination of this work and of what we have built since we first invested in the club four years ago.”

In his interview with La Gazzetta, Cardinale clarified that the new structure is also created to support the Rossoneri’s sporting ambitions: “The driving force behind operations like this is to provide Milan with the financial strength needed to compete in the transfer market and secure the best players in the world.”

There are examples of this kind of model working already. Kroenke Sports & Entertainment, AEG and Fenway Sports Group are among the most prominent and – given his background in the USA – Cardinale knows each of them well.

According to CNBC valuations, KSE was worth $26.05bn in 2026, FSG $15.37bn, and AEG $11.99bn in 2025, excluding music and hotel businesses.

KSE boasts franchises such as the Los Angeles Rams, Denver Nuggets, Colorado Avalanche and Arsenal, as well as venues such as SoFi Stadium, Ball Arena, and Emirates Stadium. The group combines sports, infrastructure and real estate development such as Hollywood Park, the district built around SoFi Stadium.

AEG – founded by Philip Anschutz – have instead built its model on the management and development of venues. It owns or manages venues such as Crypto.com Arena and The O2 in London plus the Los Angeles Kings and LA Galaxy, and operates in concert promotion and ticketing. The LA LIVE project developed around Crypto.com Arena puts the venue at the centre of a greater ecosystem.

Fenway Sports Group – born around the Boston Red Sox and Liverpool FC – have developed a holding company with interests in media, marketing, real estate, and entertainment. It’s a model Cardinale knows first hand: in 2021, RedBird invested approximately $750m in FSG, acquiring a stake of around 11%, based on an enterprise valuation of $7.35bn.

MSE in theory can harness elements of all three of these experiences: KSE’s integration of sports and infrastructure, AEG ‘s commercial development of facilities and FSG ‘s multi-sport approach. The main difference is the purpose declared by Cardinale: to use all of it to funnel money back into Milan.

From the stadium shared with Inter to the possibility of an arena in San Donato, including the new NBA Europe venture and even tennis: MSE’s scope includes various initiatives that go beyond the playing field.

The main infrastructure project is the future Generali Stadium, the new 71,500-seat facility designed by Foster + Partners and Manica. Developed jointly by the two Milanese clubs, it represents a key element of the transformation of the San Siro area and will not be a Rossoneri-only facility.

The promoters intend for the stadium to host year-round activities, from matches to concerts, as well as catering, events, and hospitality services. In other words, like the stadiums and arenas mentioned above, it will become more than just a place to go for two hours on a Sunday.

In San Donato Milanese, RedBird are also considering the possibility of building a 20,000-seat arena. Cardinale explained that the fund already owns the land and has planning permission, but the idea is also linked to Milan’s potential involvement in NBA Europe. Another area of ​​focus concerns tennis, with the possibility of hosting a tournament in the city.

Finally, RedBird intend to develop a company dedicated to managing stadiums and arenas, with services including catering, merchandising and premium hospitality. The goal is to build commercial expertise to apply to the facilities connected to the group, but also to make it available to other owners and sports clubs.

This phase will be co-ordinated by Brett Yormark, appointed CEO of MSE and set to step down as head of the Big 12 (a conference in College Football) at the end of January 2027. He worked for 14 years at Brooklyn Sports & Entertainment, overseeing the development of the Brooklyn Nets and the Barclays Center. He has also gained experience in NASCAR and Roc Nation.

The choice to go for Yormark reflects the desire to entrust the platform to someone with expertise across multiple different fields in the sporting and commercial worlds.

All these grand plans are well and good, but how will ideas turn into money that drives AC Milan forward? MSE’s economic potential is measured not only through the club’s revenues, but also through the activities that RedBird intends to develop around sports, infrastructure and entertainment.

The starting point is obviously Milan as a club, which closed the 2025-26 financial year with revenues of €464.6m, over €100m of which came from sponsorships. The main infrastructure opportunity is the new San Siro, an investment of approximately €2.3bn shared with Inter.

Projections contained in the design documents indicate a potential annual revenue of approximately €120.4m for the facility as a whole (both for the Rossoneri and the Nerazzurri), through sporting, commercial, and complementary services

These are numbers that will be revised upwards by the two clubs when considering, for example, the record agreement with Generali for naming rights. It is worth a total of €650m over 25 years, divided into €10m per year for the first five years and €30m per season for the following 20, once the stadium is built.

One of the areas on which RedBird Capital are focusing most is hospitality, which is currently worth around €15m per year for the Rossoneri. The international benchmark has already been set by Legends Global, a company Cardinale knows well.

Legends are what the Milan owner sees as a model for developing premium services, restaurants, and commercial spaces. The most obvious example is at FC Barcelona: with the support of LG, the club have marketed nearly 5,000 VIP seats at Camp Nou, generating over €380m in contracted revenue.

They aim to generate another €700m through multi-year licenses for an additional 2,000 seats. This isn’t annual revenue, but rather contracts spread over 15 or 30 years, so a guaranteed flow of money coming in that Cardinale aims to replicate.

Another agreement which demonstrates the potential of this kind of arrangement is the one with Real Madrid for the Santiago Bernabéu. It involves an investment of approximately €360m in exchange for 20-year participation in some of the stadium’s businesses,.

Legends Global also operate in facilities and events management. Following the acquisition of ASM Global (who actually proposed renovating San Siro for non-football events in Italy) in 2024, the group claims a presence in over 450 venues, approximately 20,000 events, and 165 million guests annually. Their European partnerships include Arsenal, Chelsea and Porto.

FC Barcelona launches new VIP seating licenses at Spotify Camp Nou with Legends Global

🔗 More details: https://t.co/awtEsnYE6X pic.twitter.com/iCMuM0QD35

— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) September 25, 2026

To illustrate the potential it could hold for Italy as a whole, the English subsidiary reported revenues of £131.6m in 2024, of which £105.5m came from facility and event management and £26.1m from catering. Before the integration with ASM Global, Legends had reported revenues of $1.7bn in the period ending in March 2024, with 67% coming from food and beverage sales.

In Italy, a benchmark is Forumnet, who in 2024 generated €29.7m in revenue and €12.8m in EBITDA (Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation). They manage the Assago Forum which hosts approximately 60-70 concerts a year, demonstrating how a venue can generate activity well beyond the sports calendar.

As mentioned, an arena is being planned in San Donato with an estimated investment of around €400m, which could become the basis for a Milanese franchise in NBA Europe. For reference, Olimpia Milano – the current basketball team in the city – generate around €15m through ticketing, season tickets, sponsorships and merchandising.

For NBA Europe, projections speak of over $1.5bn to be distributed to the clubs in the first six years. A theoretical division among the 12 permanent franchises would equate to approximately $20.8m per team per year, but this is not fixed yet. Entry costs – estimated by the media to be between $500m and over $1bn – also remain to be determined.

Tennis represents another potential area for development. The ATP 500 in Halle generates around €5m in revenue, excluding television rights, while the ATP Finals in Turin generate around €60m. These are events with different dimensions and scopes, but they provide a scale.

The creation of MSE has a stated objective: to strengthen Milan’s financial capacity and reduce the gap with the richest clubs on the international scene, particularly those in the Premier League.

The gap is also evident when comparing revenues. AC Milan closed the 2025-26 season with €464.6m, a significant result considering their absence from European competitions , but still far from the top English clubs.

According to the Deloitte Football Money League, in the 2024-25 season, Liverpool generated €836.1m, Arsenal €821.7m and Manchester United €793.1m. Tottenham and Chelsea also exceeded €670m and €580m, respectively.

The comparison covers different financial years, but it still shows the magnitude of the gap. Liverpool generated revenues equal to approximately 1.8 times those of Milan, while Chelsea recorded a turnover approximately €120 higher.

The chasm shows how clubs in the Premier League have showcased an ability to generate commercial revenue, enhance stadiums and reach a global audience. The gap has only been growing, and TV rights will be another focus, though that is outside of just Cardinale’s hands.

Speaking of the owner, it is now obvious he sees MSE as the name that will house the tools to try build a real sporting and commercial world around Milan. It remains to be seen how effective it will be, but the starting point is there.

#1756. Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town

There is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn

At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

Max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x

As Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a new contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

“A joy to have him,” said Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

“Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”

"He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta says Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z

Dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” said Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”

Dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

It was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” said Arteta.

Arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

Given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

The only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

Ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

Akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

"He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub

On managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta said: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”

Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:

"He'll know how to nurture him!" 🗣️Conor Coady says Mikel Arteta is the perfect manager for Max Dowman 👏 pic.twitter.com/YdgLxfKiOf

Asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta said: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”

He added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta said: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.

“Individually some big performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”

Arsenal have won the League Cup twice – in 1987 and 1993 – meaning eight clubs have better records, including Aston Villa (five titles), Tottenham Hotspur (four), Nottingham Forest (four) and Leicester City (three).

Their rather modest haul is a far cry from their record-setting 14 FA Cup titles. In the 33-years since Arsenal’s most recent League Cup triumph, the competition’s title sponsor has changed hands four times (kudos to anyone who can name all five!).

No team has scored more goals through substitutes in the Premier League than Ipswich, which is a nod to the promoted club’s depth and work in the summer transfer window.

It has meant that Gary O’Neil has had to leave established players out of match-day squads. “It was really tough leaving out Darnell [Furlong] and Anis [Mehmeti] from the squad [against Crystal Palace],” he said. “Doing that to good people is one of the toughest parts of the job. But I have faith in them, it’s just that everyone’s fit at the moment and we’ve had to recruit a strong squad to get us through an unbelievably challenging season.

“On Tuesday, whoever I pick, I have 100 per cent faith that they’re ready and that they’re going to represent what we do and how we go about it.”

On Hincapie’s omission from the match-day squad:

“Some players were carrying some fatigue, some little issues that we have to look after and some other players are available, fresh and in better conditions to play.

On Timber being left out of tonight’s squad:

“Everything is fine, but obviously he has played much more than we would have wanted. He played 53 minutes [against Sunderland] after five months. I will need to look after him.”

When asked if Arsenal will set up with a back three tonight:

Alan Davies, the actor and comedian who is a famously passionate supporter of Arsenal, recently told a story about a charity event he once attended with former captain Tony Adams. Speaking on The Tuesday Club podcast, Davies said Adams revealed his football philosophy to be: “You need seven.”

The “seven” in question, Adams explained, are seven members of the team who are ready and willing to fight the opposition in the tunnel after the game. Once a team have those seven individuals, Adams said, everything else flows from there.

For much of the past two decades, Arsenal have not had seven. In some years in the latter stages of Arsène Wenger’s tenure, they probably did not even have three or four. But that has all changed in recent seasons under Mikel Arteta, to such an extent that the Premier League champions would now undoubtedly bring considerably more than seven combatants to any touchline scrap or tunnel bust-up.

Saturday’s gritty 2-0 victory away to Sunderland provided evidence that Arsenal have added two more of these characters to their squad this summer.

Tonight will be a good test for young Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who is the latest high-class graduate of the Arsenal academy. Arsenal have extremely high hopes for Salmon, who made four senior appearances last season. He could be in the centre of defence or at right-back tonight. I suspect Ipswich striker Zian Flemming might try to target Salmon with some physical challenges, especially in the air. Let’s see how he handles it.

Ipswich Town Walton; Furlong, Kipre, Greaves, Ouattara; Florentino, Nunez; McAteer, Mehmeti, Philogene; Flemming

Substitutes Palmer, Davis, O’Shea, Walle Egeli, Enciso, Clarke, Lukic, Maeda, Akpom

Arsenal Kepa; Zubimendi, Salmon, Gabriel, Lewis-Skelly; Guimarães, Merino; Dowman, Eze, Madueke; Gyokeres

Substitutes Meslier, Calafiori, Konsa, Tzolis, Odegaard, Ibrahim, Julienne, Saka, Havertz

Max Dowman announced himself last season, showing off his gilded footwork in impressive cameos off the bench. Who could forget that lung-busting run and goal against Everton?

And while the 16-year-old winger featured in Arsenal’s pre-season, these will be his first minutes of senior football in the season proper. His only game time thus far has come in the Premier League 2 under-21s competition and he was not included in the match-day squad at the Stadium of Light on Saturday.

When asked about Dowman after the victory at Sunderland, Arteta said: “I wish we could have him here, but we have the limitation with the numbers that we can have. He will have his chance, he will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else. We know the talent that we have, we know the players that we have there and we need to help him and find a way to make sure he continues to develop and help the team.”

Although keeping Ipswich in the Premier League must be Gary O’Neil’s primary goal, he has insisted that the club will embrace opportunities in the cups.

When asked how he would approach tonight’s tie, O’Neil said: “We’ll have a strong side, we’ve worked our socks off in the transfer window to give ourselves a strong squad. Of course, a different level to Arsenal, but we’ll be strong on Tuesday and we’ll do our best to win the game.

“The club has worked so hard to have these moments and of course it’s a cup game, but to have Arsenal and Liverpool come to Portman Road a week or so apart is what everyone has worked so hard for in recent years, so we’re going to enjoy it, we’re going to have a right go and worst thing that can happen is we lose to Arsenal.”

Good evening from Portman Road, where it’s a gorgeous night for football. Ipswich have made 10 changes, which is an indication of where this competition sits in their list of priorities. Arsenal have made nine.

The Arsenal line-up is quite hard to decipher. It looks like it might be Martin Zubimendi at right-back or centre-back. I’ll keep an eye on the warm-ups and report back shortly.

Gary O’Neil wins the rotation battle, raising Arteta’s nine changes with 10 of his own. Greaves the only survivor from last weekend’s win at Selhurst Park.

Your Town tonight! ✊ pic.twitter.com/EEYjPFww4Y

Young defender Marli Salmon comes into the starting XI as Mikel Arteta makes nine changes to the team that started against Sunderland on Saturday.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Ipswich Town and Arsenal. Mikel Arteta’s side have won all six of their matches so far this season, but travel to Portman Road fresh off an incident-filled win over Sunderland which thrust officiating back into the spotlight after Ezri Konsa conceded a penalty having been – in Arteta’s words – “judo-rolled” by Dan Ballard.

After the match, the Arsenal manager said: “I watched [the incident] 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how to even think to give a penalty in this situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don’t know what to think, really. But I’m sad, that we have to discuss, after such a beautiful game, something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship… This cannot happen.”

Arteta may be pleased that VAR is not in use at this stage of the Carabao Cup, and all eyes will be on Peter Bankes who takes charge of tonight’s match against Ipswich.

This season Arsenal hope to arrest a startling League Cup record. It has been 33 years since they last lifted the trophy, during which time they have been runners-up seven times. Losing last year’s final will have also added fuel to Arsenal’s fire, and Arteta may resolve he must field a strong starting XI. In fact, he may not have much choice in his backline as Ben White has emerged as a serious injury doubt after picking up an injury at the Stadium of Light and may join Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba on the treatment table. This would likely mean starting Jurriën Timber, who is only just returning from a long-term groin issue. There is more scope for rotation in advanced positions, with Noni Madueke, Viktor Gyokeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino contenders to start.

A 90th-minute Zian Flemming winner against Crystal Palace on Saturday helped Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich to their second win in four Premier League games, a feat they required 16 matches to achieve the last time they were in the top flight. Heavy investment into Ipswich’s squad has proved fruitful thus far, though in-form striker Emersonn is expected to sit out tonight having taken a knock at Selhurst Park.

#1755. Groningen vs Heerenveen - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 19 Nov 2026 23:31

FC Groningen host SC Heerenveen in the Eredivisie at Euroborg on Saturday, November 21 in the first Derby of the North of the 2026-27 season.

Sixth-placed Heerenveen arrive on 21 points on the Eredivisie table after four consecutive league wins, while ninth-placed Groningen have taken one point from their last four games and will be without their head coach, goalkeeper and first-choice right-back.

Groningen have collected one point from their last four Eredivisie matches, a run that began with a 2-5 home defeat to Ajax on October 18 and included a 2-2 draw at NEC Nijmegen.

Those four games have cost 14 goals, and the 2-3 home loss to Sparta Rotterdam on November 1 came after Jacob Ondrejka scored after 17 seconds, before a miscommunication between Etienne Vaessen and Hans Hateboer handed Andrej Kostic the winner in the 85th minute.

The latest setback came at AZ on November 8, where De Trots van het Noorden led 3-1 after 54 minutes, lost 4-3 to a Mexx Meerdink penalty in the 91st minute and finished with nine men after Vaessen collected a second yellow card for protesting the penalty and Hateboer was sent off in the 10th minute of stoppage time for a deliberate handball.

Euroborg has offered little protection this season, with Groningen winning two, drawing one and losing three of their six home league games, and a 2-0 home defeat to Dick Lukkien’s former club FC Emmen ended their KNVB Cup run in the first round on October 29.

The recent derby record still favours the hosts, who won 2-1 at Euroborg on August 16, 2025 through a stoppage-time Brynjolfur Darri Willumsson goal and 2-0 at Abe Lenstra Stadion on January 18, 2026, when captain Thijmen Blokzijl scored the second.

The off-field story is Lukkien, who had a hip replacement last week and said the derby arrived “just too early” for his recovery, so assistant Casper Goedkoop will coach from the touchline.

Heerenveen have won four consecutive league games since a 2-0 defeat at PSV Eindhoven, beating Excelsior 4-0, ADO Den Haag 3-2, NEC Nijmegen 1-0 and Feyenoord 5-3.

Those wins have brought 13 goals and five conceded, including two from Jacob Trenskow at ADO on October 24, and have lifted De Superfriezen to 21 points from 12 games with a goal difference of +8.

The 5-3 win over Feyenoord on November 8 ended the unbeaten league record of the Eredivisie leaders, with Heerenveen recovering from 2-0 down after 31 minutes through Maas Willemsen, Levi Smans and a late Ringo Meerveld hat-trick.

Meerveld came on at half time for Maxence Rivera and scored in the 61st, 84th and 93rd minutes, with Trenskow providing the pass for the first of them.

Away from Abe Lenstra Stadion, Robin Veldman’s side have won two, drawn two and lost one of their five league trips, but they have not won in Groningen since a 2-0 victory on March 19, 2023.

Veldman said after the Feyenoord game that his players wanted to extend the run, and a win would take them further clear of seventh-placed Fortuna Sittard, who sit on 20 points.

Vaessen and Hateboer are both suspended after their red cards at AZ, so Lovro Stubljar, who has been on the bench in recent league games, is expected to start in goal and Wouter Prins should move in at right-back.

Malcolm Jeng remains out with an Achilles tendon injury and goalkeeper Rijk Janse is also sidelined, while Travis Hernes and Ryan Metu are doubtful after several weeks out.

Heerenveen have no reported injuries or suspensions, so Veldman has a full squad to choose from.

Meerveld is expected to push Rivera for a start on the left of the attacking three after his hat-trick off the bench.

Stubljar; Prins, Blokzijl, Rente, Csinger; De Jonge, Clement; Schreuders, Van Bergen, Ondrejka; Willumsson

Klaverboer; Braude, Kersten, Willemsen, Zagaritis; Linday, Courtens; Trenskow, Smans, Meerveld; Vente

Heerenveen have scored 13 goals in their last four league games and have already shown they can recover from a two-goal deficit, while Groningen have conceded at least two goals in each of their last four and lose both Vaessen and Hateboer from the back line.

Groningen have won the last two derbies and have scored at least twice in each of their last four games, so Heerenveen will concede, and the crowd will matter with Lukkien watching from home.

The gap is in defensive organisation rather than attacking quality, and a Heerenveen side with a full squad and a 13-5 goal record over four wins should edge a high-scoring derby by one goal.

#1754. Martinez insists Leverkusen must be ‘strong at the back’ against Paderborn

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Carles Martinez insisted his Bayer Leverkusen side must be "strong at the back" if they are to defeat Paderborn on Saturday.

Leverkusen have lost two of their last three Bundesliga matches, but defeated Koln 2-1 before the international break.

The Werkself lost 4-2 at home to Stuttgart following a 3-0 defeat at Hoffenheim, leaving Leverkusen fifth in the Bundesliga, five points behind Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund.

Paderborn, meanwhile, are 13th in the league after nine games, three points clear of the relegation playoff places, but also just six points behind Leverkusen.

Paderborn (W1 D3) are one of only three teams, alongside Bayern and Dortmund, to remain unbeaten in their last four Bundesliga matches.

This four-game unbeaten run equals Paderborn's club record in the Bundesliga, previously achieved only in their first four matches in the competition in 2014.

Martinez is wary of the task ahead in Paderborn, but hopes his Leverkusen players will perform in front of their home fans following the international break.

"The changes to the international break schedule are new for everyone," Martinez said.

"We've adapted well. After those gruelling weeks, we've used the time to recover and think carefully about exactly where and how we can improve.

"We can't wait to experience that special [home] atmosphere again – we've really missed it.

"Paderborn are having a good season, have a clear identity and try to dictate the play themselves. That's why we need to be particularly strong at the back. I expect the best from us."

GTA AND B04 BOTH BACK IN THE SAME WEEK!  https://t.co/3D9mcqauMV

— Bayer 04 Leverkusen (@bayer04_en) November 20, 2026

Patrik Schick has scored eight goals in the Bundesliga this season, finding the net in all four of his home appearances.

Eight goals after nine Bundesliga matchdays equals the club record for Leverkusen, previously achieved only by Schick himself (2021-22) and Patrick Helmes (2008-09).

The Czech forward has now scored as many league goals on his own as the entire Paderborn team.

Santiago Castaneda is the only Paderborn outfield player to have played every minute in the Bundesliga this season.

The American has also recorded the second-most interceptions in the league (25, Kaishu Sano: 27) and has covered the second-most distance (108.4 km, Hennes Behrens: 109.2 km).

Leverkusen have not lost any of their seven previous professional meetings with Paderborn in all competitions (W6 D1), winning each of the last six.

Against no other current Bundesliga side have Leverkusen played as many professional matches without suffering a single defeat.

Leverkusen lost 3-2 away to Elversberg on the opening matchday of the Bundesliga season and could now lose consecutive Bundesliga games against promoted sides for the first time since 2017.

However, the Werkself are unbeaten in their last 10 home Bundesliga matches against promoted teams (W7 D3).

Paderborn are one of three teams without an away win in the Bundesliga this season, alongside Koln and Union Berlin.

Paderborn have drawn three of those matches (L1), including two 0-0 draws, and have conceded only five away goals – only Dortmund have conceded fewer on the road (four).

#1753. Romano: Bruno Fernandes ‘more than a dream’ for Milan – why Amorim ‘could be crucial’

AC Milan could be a destination for Bruno Fernandes, who is thinking about leaving Manchester United to return to Italy.

It is no secret that Milan are looking at potential opportunities to bolster the attacking department, given the links with the likes of Endrick and Nicolo Tresoldi in recent days. However, there is always the possibility that Ruben Amorim might turn to players that he already knows well.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Portuguese has racked up 113 goals and 111 assists in 341 games across all competitions for United, having been their shining light in difficult recent years. He has also played in Italy before, for Novara, Udinese and Sampdoria before his switch to Sporting CP.

In a video posted on their YouTube channel last night, Matteo Moretto and Fabrizio Romano discussed the possible deals that Milan could pursue to strengthen their squad, and they commented on Fernandes.

“We can’t deny that Bruno would like to return to Italy, and the idea of ​​doing so with a big club really appeals to him. It’s true that there were contacts with AC Milan this summer, but Juventus were also reportedly interested in pursuing a possible deal for the Portuguese,” Moretto began.

“In fact, Comolli, along with Bernardo Silva, also wanted to speak more in depth with Bruno, while Juve were still in contention for the Champions League, so we’re talking about the season underway. The Bianconeri made their move before the Rossoneri.”

Romano added: “Yes, Milan also made moves to try to talk to the Portuguese, also thanks to the relationship they had with Ruben Amorim at United.

“The Rossoneri remain vigilant about the Manchester captain and didn’t want to scupper this potential move because there were so many changes and developments over the summer, first and foremost with Cardinale, who is now present and has great ambition for the club.

“Another curious anecdote I want to tell you is that, and I can say this 101%, Bruno Fernandes and Amorim have an exceptional relationship. There’s great respect between the two; Bruno wasn’t even happy about Amorim leaving Manchester.

“Clearly, there’s no concrete negotiation yet. But Amorim could be crucial for the future of Bruno Fernandes, whose contract with United is currently expiring and who still doesn’t have a clear and complete idea for his future.”

#1752. Chicago Fire vs Charlotte FC - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 19 Nov 2026 23:33

Seeking their first-ever away victory in the MLS Cup playoffs, Charlotte FC will visit SeatGeek Stadium on Sunday for game one of their best-of-three series with the Chicago Fire.

The Fire finished fourth in the Eastern Conference this year, losing their last outing 4-3 to the Columbus Crew as they wound up a point above Charlotte, who drew 3-3 with Inter Miami on Decision Day.

Throughout 2026, Chicago were out to prove that last year was no fluke as they continued to improve in the league yet again.

In his second year as head coach, Gregg Berhalter saw his team gain two more points than in his inaugural campaign, while finishing four places higher in the Eastern Conference table this time around and making the playoffs on successive occasions.

The next step will be for the Fire to find some playoff success, with this club aiming to advance beyond the first round for the first time since 2009.

During this regular season campaign, they won three more home matches when compared to 2025, though they have only won one playoff fixture in Illinois since 2009, defeating Orlando City 3-1 in the Wildcard Round a year ago.

They have points in three of their last four MLS encounters but will try to snap a two-match domestic losing run at home this weekend, conceding a combined seven goals in those two defeats.

On Sunday, the Fire can beat Charlotte at home for a third consecutive occasion, having won those last two contests by a single goal.

The Crown are back in the post-season for a third successive occasion, hoping to get past round one at long last.

Dean Smith’s men set a single-season club record for goals scored in 2026 (66), averaging just under two per match (1.9) in the league this year.

This weekend, they will hope to end a four-match domestic winless run away from home and collect their first-ever road triumph in the post-season.

Defensively, they have been shaky as the visitors in 2026, conceding three or more goals on eight occasions in the regular season.

In round one of the playoffs, they have netted just one goal overall and have never scored in the opening half of an MLS road playoff game.

Charlotte have also never won a post-season game in normal time, and have scored first only once, in 2024 when they lost to Orlando City on penalties in the decisive third game of that best-of-three opening round series.

Due to a knock, Inter Miami loanee Noah Allen is questionable for the Fire, as is Robin Lod, who has a leg injury.

Robert Lewandowski has three goals in his last two games, netting a brace in their defeat to the Crew, with Maren Haile-Selassie also scoring on Decision Day.

On the Charlotte side, Tim Ream is questionable as he recovers from an adductor issue, Archie Goodwin may not be available due to a foot problem, Nimfasha Berchimas is recovering from foot surgery and Aron John is dealing with a shoulder injury.

Liel Abada notched a pair of goals in their regular-season finale, while a 90th-minute strike from Rodolfo Aloko earned them a point against the reigning MLS Cup champions.

#1751. Sheffield United vs Watford - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 23:37

Aiming to break into the top eight of the Championship table on their return from the November international break, Sheffield United will welcome Watford to Bramall Lane on Saturday.

The hosts lost in their final game before the break but sit just two points outside of the playoff spots, while their visitors sit five points above the drop zone thanks to a win and a draw in their last two outings.

Sheffield United head back into Championship action after the international break on Saturday aiming to reignite their pursuit of the playoff places.

Aiming to kick on from a 13th-placed finish in 2025-26 and challenge for a return to the Premier League, the Blades experienced a mixed start to the season but looked to have turned a corner after the September and October break.

The Blades managed four wins and one draw in their first six games back from that break, scoring 11 goals and conceding six in those games, culminating in a 1-0 home victory over Wrexham, with Ben Brereton Diaz on the scoresheet, and a 3-2 away victory against Preston North End thanks to Sydie Peck's hat-trick.

They were unable to carry that winning streak into the latest break, though, visiting Charlton Athletic last time out and losing 2-1, having fallen behind and levelled through Jordan Ayew before Matt Godden scored the winner for their hosts 10 minutes from time.

Now sat 10th but just two points behind seventh and eighth spots, Sheffield United will again hope to come back firing and return to winning ways at Bramall Lane on Saturday.

Their visitors, meanwhile, head to South Yorkshire aiming to build on a positive turn in form before the break.

After a 16th-placed Championship finish in 2025-26 and the summer appointment of Alessio Dionisi, Watford endured a poor start to the new campaign, picking up just 11 points from their first 13 matches, winning three and losing eight of those.

The Hornets' away record is a real cause for concern, having lost six and drawn one of their seven league matches on the road, scoring just four goals in those and conceding 14.

The most recent of those was a 3-2 away loss against Norwich City, in which they led 2-0 at the break, but Dionisi's men did bounce back, beating Lincoln City 1-0 at home thanks to Stephy Mavididi's goal, before they hosted then-leaders Middlesbrough last time out and stood strong for a point from a 0-0 draw.

Watford now return to action hoping to add to those positive results and extend their five-point lead over the relegation zone.

Sheffield Wednesday are unable to call on defender Femi Seriki, who sustained a long-term injury before the break, while Matt Doherty, Ryan One and Joe Rothwell may also remain sidelined.

Patrick Bamford may be in line for a return, though, having been out with a shoulder injury, and if deemed fit he could return up front from the start despite competition for those places from Ben Brereton Diaz, Tom Cannon, Jordan Ayew and Tyrese Campbell.

Kalvin Phillips has impressed in his second loan spell with the Blades thus far and will again join Sydie Peck in midfield.

Watford are still without Kwadwo Baah, Jeremy Ngakia, Soumaila Coulibaly and Edoardo Bove on Saturday due to ongoing injuries.

Kevin Keben and Branimir Mlacic should again join Mattie Pollock in the middle of the defence after their clean sheet against Middlesbrough last time out, while Krepin Diatta may start in a wing-back role if he is fit after being forced off in that game.

Competition for attacking spots is rife with Mamadou Doumbia, Amin Nabizada, Stephy Mavididi, Luca Kjerrumgaard, Rocco Vata and Othmane Maamma all pushing to start, while Myron Boadu has often led the line but missed the Middlesbrough game.

Sheffield United possible starting lineup:

Cooper; Choudhury, Tanganga, Kitching, Burrows; Donovan, Peck, Phillips, Brereton Diaz; Cannon, Bamford

Ravaglia; Diatta, Keben, Pollock, Mlacic, Zemura; Kayembe, Kyprianou, Bravo; Mavididi, Doumbia

Watford showed signs of improvement before the break with consecutive clean sheets, but we fancy Sheffield United, rested after a disappointing defeat halted their notable improvement, to bounce back at Bramall Lane.
